steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Textile traditions carry deep cultural meaning — African wax prints, Indian block printing, Japanese shibori, Scandinavian knitting each tell stories of place and identity.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Contemporary textile designers draw on tradition while innovating — understanding history enriches your own creative decisions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sustainability and ethics in textiles: consider material sourcing, dye pollution, fast fashion, fair trade and waste reduction.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Your research should INSPIRE your own work — adapt traditional techniques for contemporary purposes, do not just reproduce them.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring textile designers and traditions. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with textile designers and traditions. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with textile designers and traditions. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to textile designers and traditions, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
